title: Rep2Vec: Repository Embedding via Heterogeneous Graph Adversarial Contrastive Learning

problem.claim: Repository representations are needed for applications such as malicious repository detection on GitHub.

gap.claim: Existing methods mainly focus on code content, overlook relational data among repositories, and typically require substantial labeled data while neglecting unlabeled data.

contributions.claim: Rep2Vec integrates code content, structural relations, and unlabeled data to learn repository representations.
The method builds a repository heterogeneous graph encoded by a graph neural network and uses adversarial contrastive learning across node and meta-path views.
The method combines adversarial-graph and original-graph contrastive learning, then fine-tunes the encoder for downstream tasks with knowledge distillation.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe Rep2Vec as a novel model.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Extensive experiments on a collected GitHub dataset demonstrate the effectiveness of Rep2Vec compared with state-of-the-art methods across multiple repository tasks.

narrative_sequence.summary: The growth of open-source software and Git-based development has produced substantial repository data on social coding platforms, including GitHub.
Repository representation tools have been developed for related applications such as malicious repository detection.
Prior methods underuse repository relations and unlabeled data while often requiring many labeled examples.
Rep2Vec models heterogeneous repository structure and trains representations with adversarial, multi-view contrastive learning, followed by downstream fine-tuning and knowledge distillation.
The authors report effectiveness on multiple repository tasks using a collected GitHub dataset and comparisons with state-of-the-art methods.

source_observation.claim: Repository representation learning can combine code content, structural relations, and unlabeled data.

interpretation.claim: Useful representations may improve when both content and relational structure are modeled while reducing dependence on labeled data.

application.claim: For repository-analysis tasks, consider heterogeneous graphs and semi-supervised or contrastive representation learning.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish which tasks, datasets, or settings benefit most from these design choices.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the collected dataset size, composition, or task definitions.
The abstract does not report quantitative results, ablations, or implementation details.
